blogs.title: Demystifying Orthogonal Finetuning: How a Simple Rotation Keeps Diffusion Models In Control
blogs.description: A beginner-friendly walkthrough of the core idea behind Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): keeping the angles between neurons fixed while fine‑tuning a large diffusion model. The post explains why preserving neuron directions on the unit hypersphere is key to maintaining a model’s semantic knowledge, and shows how a single layer‑shared orthogonal matrix turns complex weight adjustments into a smooth rotation.

blogs.title: Subject‑Driven Generation Made Easy with OFT: Fast, Stable, and Identity‑Preserving
blogs.description: An exploration of how OFT transforms the DreamBooth workflow for subject‑driven image generation. Readers will see real‑world comparisons of convergence speed, stability, and subject identity preservation versus traditional LoRA or vanilla fine‑tuning, along with practical tips on setting epochs and learning rates.

blogs.title: Controllable Text‑to‑Image Generation: From Canny Edges to Realistic Scenes with Constrained OFT
blogs.description: A deep dive into the controllable generation use case. The article covers how Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT) enables precise image edits using edge maps or segmentation inputs, introduces the new control consistency metric, and demonstrates why COFT outperforms ControlNet and T2I‑Adapter in both speed and quality.

blogs.title: Parameter Efficiency Unpacked: Why OFT Learns Faster Than LoRA or Adapter Libraries
blogs.description: This post breaks down the math behind OFT’s parameter count using block‑diagonal orthogonal matrices, compares it head‑to‑head with LoRA’s low‑rank updates, and explains why OFT’s full‐rank but structured update gives a better trade‑off between flexibility and regularity.

blogs.title: Future Directions for Orthogonal Finetuning: Beyond Image Generation
blogs.description: Looking ahead, we sketch three exciting research avenues hinted at in the paper: speeding up Cayley vs. matrix inverse operations, exploring compositionality of multiple orthogonal transforms across tasks, and designing even more bias‑free parameterizations to push OFT’s efficiency further.
